cells.Values and default: Exactly `1` turns the statistics on. Any other text, also empty text, leaves them off and logs one warning per process. Unset: off, and no message is logged. Empty: off, and one warning is logged.
cells.Effect: Turns on the attention path statistics. They count the attention work on 3 paths: the AVX loop and the AMX kernel on the CPU, and the FPGA cards. Lines that start with `[attn-stats]` go to stderr when a model state (the run-time object of a loaded model) is destroyed. No flag exists. When on, the info log shows `attention path stats on (TRON_ATTN_STATS=1) for model`. The FUSE stats file `/model/<model id>/attention/summary` shows `"on":true`. Per-layer and per-worker files exist only when on. The stderr lines appear only when work was counted. `README.stats.md` describes the output.

cells.Effect: Selects the socket through which the process sends trace events to `traced` (the Perfetto daemon). The socket is then not used. Tron does not log the socket name.

cells.Values and default: The exact text `traced`, or a file path. The text is not checked at startup. Unset: the destination is `traced`, the Perfetto system daemon. An outside Perfetto client owns the output file. Empty: the first `SIGUSR1` capture aborts the program.
cells.Effect: With a file path, a `SIGUSR1` capture is recorded inside the process and written to that file. cells.Values and default: Exactly `1` or `true` turns the sampler on. The comparison is case-sensitive. Any other text is off. No message is logged. Unset: off. No sampler thread is created. A trace holds no counters of the category `hw`.
cells.Effect: Turns on the hardware sampler. When a trace session starts, the process creates one sampler thread. While the trace records the category `hw`, the thread reads CPU temperature, CPU frequency and package power from `/sys` and writes them to the Perfetto trace as counters. It has an effect only when a trace starts. The script `perfetto/grant-rapl-read` accepts the same 2 values. It then uses `sudo` to give all local users read access to the RAPL files (CPU energy counters) under `/sys/class/powercap`. Package power needs that access.

cells.Values and default: Integer count of tokens, parsed with `atoi`. A negative number counts as `0`. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. Unset: `0` tokens. The trace starts when prompt parsing completes.
cells.Effect: With `runtron --trace-gen FILE`, the trace starts when the prompt tokens plus the generated tokens of a request reach the value. A value at or below the prompt length starts the trace when prompt parsing completes. Only `--trace-gen` without `--trace-passes` uses the value. `--trace` ignores it. With `--trace-passes`, runtron logs the warning `--trace-passes overrides TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN`. If no request reaches the value, the trace starts and ends when the first request finishes. The value is read once per process.

rows.name: DICE_ADMIN_GROUP
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Set by: A person, in the environment of the Dice daemon.
cells.Values and default: The name of a Unix group. A name that does not exist gives no extra rights and no error. Unset: only root and the user that runs the daemon are Dice administrators.
cells.Effect: Members of the group become Dice administrators. An administrator can cancel the submissions (commands that Dice queues or runs) of other users, attach to them and see their full details. An administrator can also stop the daemon. The daemon reads its own environment at each request. A value in the environment of a client has no effect. The daemon takes the user id of the client from the socket. The packaged `dice.service` does not set the variable.

rows.name: DICE_BOX_SLOTS
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Set by: A person, in the environment of the Dice daemon or `bin/slice`.
cells.Values and default: Integer greater than 0, parsed with `int()`. Other text, `0` or a negative number ends the program with an error. Unset: `SLICE_BOX_CAPACITY` is used. If that is also unset, the count comes from `config/resource-map.yaml`.
cells.Effect: Sets the number of slots of the server. The Dice daemon schedules over that many slots. `bin/slice` uses it as the total slot count. The daemon reads it once at startup. The daemon option `--box` takes priority. The packaged `dice.service` sets neither. On a shared host `bin/slice` first asks the running daemon for the count. It reads the variable only when that fails or when `DICE_DISABLE` is `1`.

hints.problem: The two variables have the same meaning, and the row of `SLICE_BOX_CAPACITY` says so. Their Set by cells follow different conventions. One names the test fixtures and the other does not, although the Dice test fixture sets `DICE_BOX_SLOTS`.
hints.suggested: Replace the Set by cell of `DICE_BOX_SLOTS` with: "A person, in the environment of the Dice daemon or `bin/slice`. Dice test fixtures also set it."
